plan.summary: Replace the broken bool(value) call with a module-level immutable token table (dict constant) that maps exactly the two accepted tokens to their boolean values, eliminating branching and fixing the false-case regression.
steps: Identify that bool('false') is True in Python, causing the registered check to fail
Replace the branching/truthiness logic with a module-level constant dict mapping 'true'→True and 'false'→False
Make parse_enabled a simple table lookup that raises KeyError for any unrecognised token (no new tokens accepted)
Verify the registered check parser-contract passes for both 'true' and 'false'
risks: Any caller passing an empty string or other token will now get KeyError instead of a silent True/False; this is the intended stricter contract
The dict is technically mutable at runtime (Python limitation), but it is treated as a frozen constant by convention and naming

answer.summary: Refactored parse_enabled to use a module-level immutable token table (_TOKENS) instead of branching/truthiness, fixing the false-case regression while accepting no new tokens.
